nodes.content: Develop long-tail image recognition that preserves rare-class accuracy when predictive background correlations reverse without target-domain labels.
requirements: Improve bottom-quintile class macro-accuracy by 5 percentage points over empirical risk minimization under background reversals.
Keep top-quintile class macro-accuracy within 1 percentage point of that baseline using identical training data.

nodes.content: Train class-balanced foreground prototypes with pseudo-masked source background swaps, distilling head-class logits from a frozen ERM model.
What pseudo-mask foreground recall is needed for background swaps to preserve rare-class cues while head-logit distillation protects head classes?
At ≥85% foreground-mask recall, swaps raise reversal-set tail macro-accuracy ≥5 points versus ERM; distillation limits head loss ≤1 point.
Audit 200 source masks; sweep pseudo-mask thresholds around 85% recall and distillation strength; compare BackgroundFlip-LT quintile macro-accuracy with ERM.
Audit 200 source masks, train 80/85/90%-recall swap variants at two distillation weights, and score BackgroundFlip-LT quintile macro-accuracy.
On BackgroundFlip-LT, 85%-recall swaps with distillation yielded tail macro-accuracy 34% versus ERM’s 28%, and head 71.5% versus 72%.
Select 85%-recall swaps with head-logit distillation, given BackgroundFlip-LT’s 6-point tail gain and 0.5-point head loss versus ERM.
BackgroundFlip-LT mask-sweep report containing the 200-mask audit, six swap–distillation configurations, per-quintile macro-accuracy, and ERM comparisons.
Using the mask-sweep report, test 85%-recall swaps plus distillation on unseen BackgroundFlip-LT reversals, measuring three-seed quintile macro-accuracy versus ERM.
On unseen BackgroundFlip-LT reversals, three-seed tail macro-accuracy was 29% versus ERM’s 28%; head was 71.5% versus 72%.
≥95%-recall, ≤5%-leakage masks should improve unseen-reversal tail macro-accuracy ≥5 points versus ERM, with distillation limiting head loss ≤1 point.
Refine source-only pseudo-masks toward ≥95% recall and ≤5% leakage; retrain swaps with distillation and compare unseen-reversal quintile accuracy against ERM.
At 95% mask recall and 4% leakage, unseen-reversal tail macro-accuracy reached 34% versus ERM’s 28%; head, 71.4% versus 72%.
Train source-only background-cluster group DRO with rare-class weighting and ERM-logit regularization on frequent classes.
Cluster source backgrounds, train rare-weighted group DRO with head-logit regularization, then compare unseen-reversal quintile macro-accuracy against identical-data ERM.
Use the mask-sweep report’s audited masks to extract source backgrounds; cluster them and train rare-weighted group DRO with head-logit regularization.
Source-background group manifest with cluster assignments, rare-class weights, and training configuration for head-regularized group DRO.
Audit manifest cluster assignments and weights; compare group DRO, refined foreground swaps, and ERM on unseen BackgroundFlip-LT quintile macro-accuracy.
On newly held-out BackgroundFlip-LT reversal clusters, group DRO tail/head macro-accuracy: 35%/71.3%; refined swaps: 30%/71.4%; ERM: 28%/72%.
Does group DRO’s 7-point tail gain persist for rare classes represented in fewer than three source-background clusters?
For rare classes spanning fewer than three source-background clusters, group DRO’s tail macro-accuracy gain falls below 5 points versus ERM.
Using the source-background group manifest, compare group DRO’s ERM-relative rare-class macro-accuracy for <3 versus ≥3 source-cluster classes on held-out reversals.
On held-out reversals, <3-cluster rare classes scored 30% macro-accuracy versus ERM’s 28%; ≥3-cluster classes scored 40% versus 28%.
Using the group manifest, restrict rare classes to two clusters; retrain group DRO and ERM identically and compare reversal macro-accuracy.
In controlled two-cluster retraining, group DRO achieved 34% rare-class reversal macro-accuracy versus ERM’s 28%, a 6-point gain.
For rare classes with fewer than three clusters, group DRO retains ≥5-point gains when each cluster contains ≥20 training images.
Using the group manifest, stratify <3-cluster rare classes by minimum cluster size (≥20 versus <20); compare reversal macro-accuracy against ERM.
Among <3-cluster rare classes, minimum cluster size ≥20 yielded 34% reversal macro-accuracy versus ERM’s 28%; <20 yielded 27% versus 28%.
Fill sparse rare-class background clusters to 20 images using ≥95%-recall source-only swaps; train group DRO with head-logit distillation.
Do source-only swaps filling sparse rare-class clusters to 20 images restore ≥5-point tail gains without exceeding 1-point head loss?
Filling rare-class clusters to 20 images with ≥95%-recall swaps yields ≥5-point tail gain and ≤1-point head loss versus ERM.
Fill sparse clusters to 20 images with audited swaps; compare hybrid, unfilled group DRO, and ERM on reversal tail/head macro-accuracy.
Using the group manifest, fill <3-cluster rare-class groups to 20 with ≥95%-recall swaps; compare hybrid, unfilled DRO, ERM tail/head accuracies.
Hybrid achieved 36%/71.4% tail/head macro-accuracy versus ERM’s 28%/72%; filled sparse-class accuracy rose from 27% unfilled to 34%.
BackgroundFlip-LT hybrid evaluation bundle with source-only cluster-fill manifest, ≥95%-recall mask audit, model checkpoint, and ERM-matched quintile scores.
Using the hybrid bundle, audit source-only provenance and evaluate three-seed tail/head macro-accuracy on disjoint BackgroundFlip-LT reversals against ERM.
On disjoint BackgroundFlip-LT reversals, three-seed hybrid tail/head macro-accuracy averaged 35%/71.3% versus ERM’s 28%/72%; provenance audit confirmed source-only training.
Using the hybrid bundle, ablate head-logit distillation and reduce cluster-fill targets to 10 images; measure reversal tail/head macro-accuracy.
On texture-only reversals, hybrid tail accuracy was 31% versus ERM’s 28%; 10-fill reached 29%, undistilled head 69% versus 72%.
Are sparse clusters filled with texture-homogeneous backgrounds despite semantic diversity, explaining the hybrid’s 3-point tail gain on texture-only reversals?
Four texture modes per 20-image filled cluster should yield ≥5-point texture-reversal tail gain versus ERM and ≤1-point head loss.
Using the hybrid bundle, audit fill-texture diversity, rebalance each 20-image cluster across four modes, and score texture-reversal quintiles versus ERM.
Audit found 78% of filled clusters single-mode; four-mode texture-reversal tail/head accuracy reached 34%/71.3% versus ERM’s 28%/72%.
Retain the distilled hybrid’s disjoint-reversal gains, but require four-mode, 20-image fills to address its texture-reversal failure.
Train texture-stratified group DRO with four-mode, 20-image source-only rare-cluster fills and ERM head-logit distillation.
Build source-only four-mode fills, retrain distilled texture-stratified group DRO, and validate quintile macro-accuracy on disjoint semantic and texture reversals.
Using the source-background manifest and four-mode audit, fill sparse rare-class clusters to 20 images across four textures; train distilled DRO.
Texture-stratified DRO checkpoint and source-only fill manifest recording each rare-class cluster’s 20 images, four texture modes, and distillation settings.
Audit the checkpoint’s fill manifest; compare three-seed bottom/top-quintile macro-accuracy with identical-data ERM on disjoint semantic and texture reversals.
Source-only audit passed; three-seed semantic and texture reversal tail/head macro-accuracy: 35%/71.3% and 34%/71.2%; ERM: 28%/72% on both.
Using the checkpoint and fill manifest, test joint semantic–texture reversals against identical-data ERM across three seeds, auditing tail/head macro-accuracy.
On joint semantic–texture reversals, three-seed tail/head macro-accuracy was 31%/71.1% versus ERM’s 28%/72%, missing the 5-point tail target.
Do four-mode fills undersample semantic–texture combinations, leaving rare classes exposed when both background cues reverse together?
Balancing 20-image fills across eight semantic–texture cells, ≥2 images per cell, should restore ≥5-point joint-reversal tail gains versus ERM.
Audit checkpoint fills; rebalance eight source-only semantic–texture cells to ≥2 images each, retrain, and score joint-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy versus ERM.
With ≥2 images in every semantic–texture cell, joint-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy reached 32%/71.2% versus ERM’s 28%/72%.
Joint-cue reliance, not cell undersampling, drives failure; paired-swap foreground consistency should yield ≥5-point tail gain, ≤1-point head loss.
Using the checkpoint, measure paired-swap prediction agreement, add foreground-consistency loss, and evaluate joint-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy against ERM.
Paired-swap agreement rose from 62% to 84%; joint-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy reached 34%/71.2% versus ERM’s 28%/72%.
Adopt paired-swap foreground consistency atop texture-stratified DRO: joint-reversal tail gains 6 points with 0.8-point head loss; cell balancing insufficient.
